newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks fall in early trade on Deng worries.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks fall in early trade on Deng worries.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell in morning trade on Tuesday as concerns about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping returned to plague the market.
The index fell 130.89 points to an early low of 13,013.73 before paring its losses later to trade down 60.17 points, or 0.46 percent, at 13,084.45.
Turnover was HK$1.28 billion after the first half hour of trade. February index futures fell 105 points to 13,100.
Sources said on Monday that Deng's deteriorating health had forced Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin and other leaders to cut short provincial trips to return to Beijing.

"I think in the short term the market will continue to be plagued by speculation of the deterioration of Deng's health and that will keep investors on the sidelines," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
"The market might make use of this as an excuse for further consolidation," he said.
Concerns about Deng's health contributed to a 547-point slide in the Hang Seng Index last week. Analysts said support should be found around 13,000 points.
Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities, said investors were not rushing to sell.
"The market is likely to trade sideways over the next couple of days," he said.
"There is still some worry about Deng Xiaoping, whether his death is imminent or not. I don't think it is going to have a lasting impact on China's policy or on the stock market," Rossiter added.
Among the major blue chips, HSBC Holdings shed HK$1.00 to HK$183.50 and Hang Seng Bank fell HK$0.25 to HK$88.00.
Cheung Kong fell HK$0.25 to HK$72.25 and Henderson Land was down HK$0.75 at HK$68.75.

Shares in Hutchison Whampoa fell HK$0.25 to HK$56.50. The company said it would book an exceptional profit of HK$1.24 billion from the disposal of its stake in Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd to Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd.
It also said its unaudited consolidated profit for the four-month period to October 31, 1996, amounted to about HK$2.98 billion.
